molecular_water_reorganization.summary: Using ultrafast X‑ray spectroscopy and scattering, researchers visualized how water molecules rearrange as a proton‑electron transfer reaction proceeds, revealing unprecedented structural detail.
highlights: Ultrafast X‑ray methods at the Linac Coherent Light Source captured simultaneous electron and proton dynamics
Combined X‑ray absorption (chemRIXS) and scattering (XCS) revealed solvent reorganization around a ruthenium complex
Quantum chemistry and molecular dynamics simulations interpreted the transient X‑ray signals
Findings published in Nature Communications suggest pathways to more efficient catalysts and flow batteries

nano_sandwich_photocathode_co2_to_ethano.headline: Nano‑sandwich Photocathode Boosts Solar CO₂‑to‑Ethanol Conversion Efficiency
nano_sandwich_photocathode_co2_to_ethano.summary: A Charles University team created a Cu₂O‑MXene‑TiO₂ nano‑sandwich photocathode that converts CO₂ to pure ethanol with a record 2.74% solar‑energy efficiency.
highlights: Record solar‑energy‑to‑ethanol conversion efficiency of 2.74% achieved in lab tests.
MXene‑TiO₂ layer stabilizes Cu₂O, preventing degradation for many hours under illumination.
The system produces only ethanol, eliminating mixed by‑products and simplifying downstream processing.
Photocathode fabricated on FTO substrate using controlled heating to form ultrathin TiO₂ coating.
Research published in Advanced Energy Materials (2026) and led by Pavla Eliášová.

universe_acceleration_analysis_2026.headline: New Study Confirms Cosmic Acceleration, Refutes Recent Slowdown Claim
universe_acceleration_analysis_2026.summary: A fresh analysis of Type Ia supernova data shows the universe’s expansion is still accelerating, overturning a prior study that suggested a deceleration.
highlights: The paper, published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, re‑examines host‑galaxy age assumptions.
Lead author Dr Phil Wiseman (University of Southampton) found the earlier Korean analysis mis‑treated galaxy and stellar ages.
Including host‑galaxy mass corrections restores the original evidence for dark‑energy‑driven acceleration.
The work involves Nobel laureates Prof Adam Riess and Prof Brian Schmidt, reinforcing the robustness of supernova cosmology.

galapagos_corals_el_nino_intensity.headline: Modern El Niño Events Outpace Past Millennium, Galápagos Coral Study Shows
galapagos_corals_el_nino_intensity.summary: Coral records from the Galápagos reveal that El Niño events in the last 40 years are stronger than any in the past thousand years, linking intensification to human‑caused warming.
highlights: El Niño intensity in the past 40 years exceeds all recorded events over the previous millennium
Coral oxygen‑isotope and strontium‑to‑calcium ratios provide monthly temperature reconstructions
The 1982–83 and 1997–98 El Niños match the strongest signals in the new coral dataset
Findings, published in Science, align recent ocean thermometer data with long‑term coral evidence

free_falling_atoms_gravity_test.headline: Free‑falling rubidium atoms on Tiangong confirm Galileo’s gravity test to 0.05 thousandths of a percent
free_falling_atoms_gravity_test.summary: Scientists on China’s Tiangong space station observed two clouds of rubidium atoms with different neutron counts falling at virtually identical rates, validating the weak equivalence principle with unprecedented precision.
highlights: Two rubidium atom clouds with differing nuclear masses fell with matching accelerations
The measured agreement reached a precision of 0.05 thousandths of a percent
Results support the equivalence of gravitational and inertial mass, a cornerstone of general relativity

protein_brake_nerve_repair.headline: Blocking AHR Unlocks Nerve Regeneration in Mice After Injury
protein_brake_nerve_repair.summary: Researchers at Icahn School of Medicine found that inhibiting the aryl hydrocarbon receptor enables damaged axons to regrow, improving movement and sensation in mouse models.
highlights: AHR acts as a brake that suppresses axon growth after injury
Pharmacological or genetic AHR inhibition restored axon regeneration in peripheral nerve and spinal cord injury mice
Regeneration was linked to increased protein synthesis and HIF‑1α‑driven repair pathways

plastic_weld_memory_strength.headline: Polyethylene Welds Remember Surface Orientation, Boosting Pipe Joint Strength
plastic_weld_memory_strength.summary: Computer simulations reveal that polyethylene welds retain a molecular memory of their original surfaces, creating extra crystal growth that makes joints stiffer than surrounding pipe material.
highlights: Molecular dynamics simulations modeled millions of polyethylene chains during heating and cooling
Residual surface orientation seeds additional crystallization at the weld line
The reinforced weld pushes failure into the softer surrounding pipe, enhancing overall strength
Effect persists with recycled polyethylene, supporting sustainable pipe construction

natural_hydrogen_generation.headline: Western Australia’s Iron‑Rich Rocks Could Yield Massive Natural Hydrogen
natural_hydrogen_generation.summary: Researchers at Edith Cowan University found that magnetite in Western Australia’s Pilbara formations can naturally produce hydrogen, a process that can be amplified for large‑scale energy use.
highlights: Magnetite releases hydrogen when reacted with hot water at 200 °C under high pressure.
Injecting a solution into banded iron formations increased hydrogen output in laboratory tests.
Rock permeability and fractures control water access, influencing hydrogen generation efficiency.
The study appears in the International Journal of Hydrogen Energy, 2026.

sleep_micro_awakenings_alzheimers_risk.headline: Micro‑Awakenings During Sleep Signal Higher Alzheimer Risk in Middle‑Age Adults
sleep_micro_awakenings_alzheimers_risk.summary: Frequent brief nighttime micro‑awakenings were linked to elevated polygenic Alzheimer risk among healthy adults aged 50‑69, suggesting an early sleep‑based warning sign.
highlights: Study of >500 participants found a correlation between micro‑awakening frequency and Alzheimer polygenic risk in the 50‑69 age
The association was absent in younger adults (18‑31), indicating an age‑dependent effect.
Locus coeruleus integrity, examined with 7‑Tesla MRI, related to REM sleep quality and may underlie the observed link.

hominin_pelvis.institution: Various (research team reported in Live Science)
hominin_pelvis.headline: Homo floresiensis pelvis shows human‑like bipedalism, but slower and short‑range
hominin_pelvis.summary: Study of the LB 1 hip bones reveals the extinct “hobbit” walked upright similarly to modern humans, yet without speed or long‑distance capability.
highlights: Pelvic analysis of LB 1 matches Pleistocene Homo species such as Homo erectus
Iliac flare measurement indicates less efficient, slower bipedal gait
Findings suggest limited travel distances and possible arboreal activity

low_temp_graphene_growth.headline: Low‑Temperature Graphene Synthesis on Cerium Oxide Enables Sustainable Carbon Recycling
low_temp_graphene_growth.summary: Researchers at Tohoku University and Queen Mary University of London produced graphene and related carbon materials at just 300 °C using acetylene on cerium oxide, opening eco‑friendly recycling pathways.
highlights: Graphene grown at 300 °C on CeO₂ nanoparticles via acetylene CVD
Temperature tuning yields quantum‑dot, aggregated, and porous graphene forms
Acetylene feedstock can be sourced from waste gases, biomass, and recycled plastics

new_vector_based_ai_model.headline: Pathway’s BDH‑CQ Model Cuts AI Reasoning Costs Up to Eleven‑Fold Compared to GPT 5.6 Luna
new_vector_based_ai_model.summary: A new post‑transformer AI from Pathway, BDH‑CQ, solves non‑verbal ARC‑AGI‑1 puzzles at 30% accuracy while using roughly one‑eleventh the token cost of OpenAI’s GPT 5.6 Luna model.
highlights: BDH‑CQ achieved a 30% score on the ARC‑AGI‑1 benchmark, solving three of ten puzzles in two attempts
The model runs on just 150 million parameters, far fewer than Llama 3 70B or Llama 3.1 405B
Token usage is about 11 times lower than GPT 5.6 Luna, dramatically reducing operational expenses

mrna_polya_tail_gastruloids.headline: mRNA deadenylase Cnot8 controls body‑plan patterning in mouse gastruloids
mrna_polya_tail_gastruloids.summary: A single‑cell CRISPR screen shows that loss of Cnot8 elongates poly(A) tails, stabilising transcripts and diverting mesoderm toward ectopic notochord fate.
highlights: Cnot8 loss triggers genome‑wide poly(A) tail elongation and transcript stabilization
Mesodermal cells in Cnot8‑deficient gastruloids adopt ectopic notochord identity
Axial patterning is dramatically altered, linking deadenylation to morphogen signaling

human_d3_receptor_structure.headline: Crystal Structure of Human Dopamine D3 Receptor Reveals Antagonist Binding Details
human_d3_receptor_structure.summary: Scientists have resolved the human dopamine D3 receptor structure at 3.15 Å with the selective antagonist eticlopride, shedding light on ligand interactions.
highlights: Structure solved at 3.15 Å resolution
Eticlopride bound in the orthosteric pocket
Intracellular loop 2 adopts two distinct conformations

airborne_tb_mutation.headline: Drying Airborne TB Bacteria Mutate, Revealing New Drug Target
airborne_tb_mutation.summary: Researchers found that desiccation triggers DNA repair in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, increasing rifampin‑resistance mutations and identifying the Mfd gene as a therapeutic target.
highlights: Desiccation induces oxidative DNA damage in airborne Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
The DNA repair protein Mfd promotes survival and rifampin‑resistance mutations during drying.
Silencing Mfd reduces survival of drug‑resistant TB in aerosol experiments.
Analysis of >50,000 TB genomes shows fewer rifampin‑resistance mutations in strains with Mfd alterations.

diamond_ice_giant.headline: Diamond Melt Experiment Solves Ice Giant Mystery and Boosts Fusion Yield
diamond_ice_giant.summary: LLNL scientists used Omega Laser shocks to melt diamond, confirming its melting point and revealing conditions for diamond rain on Neptune, while suggesting a three‑fold fusion boost.
highlights: Diamond melted at >1 TPa pressures and sun‑like temperatures for a billionth of a second
Measured melting point matches modern quantum‑physics models, resolving a 20‑year discrepancy
Solid diamond is less dense than liquid metallic carbon, enabling diamond rain in ice‑giant interiors
Gentler shock could triple inertial‑confinement‑fusion energy output according to calculations

mass_of_universe_measurement.headline: University of Missouri Team Finds Initial Mass Function Varies Across Star Clusters, Challenging Universal
mass_of_universe_measurement.summary: A new study using Gaia data shows that the stellar initial mass function differs among clusters, implying galaxy mass estimates may need revision.
highlights: Initial mass function (IMF) shows distinct mass ratios in different star clusters
Gaia satellite data of ~2 billion Milky Way stars underpins the analysis
University of Missouri researchers propose environment‑specific IMF models

ocean_heat_content_uncertainty_reduction.headline: Six‑fold Cut in Ocean Heat Content Uncertainty Since 1960
ocean_heat_content_uncertainty_reduction.summary: A new large‑ensemble analysis shows global upper‑2000 m ocean heat content uncertainty fell from ~111 ZJ to ~19 ZJ over six decades.
highlights: Uncertainty dropped six‑fold from ~111 ZJ (1955‑1965) to ~19 ZJ (2014‑2023)
Mapping and sampling errors now dominate the reduced uncertainty budget
Quality‑Control errors have become the primary source of recent uncertainty
Upper‑2000 m heat increase since 1955 is robust at 449 [385, 519] ZJ

5.headline: Deep‑Sleep Brain Waves Linked to Slower Alzheimer’s Progression, Study Finds
5.summary: In a Neurology paper, researchers found that stronger NREM sleep spindles and slow oscillations mitigate the negative impact of high CSF orexin on Alzheimer’s decline over three years.
highlights: 60 participants with mild‑to‑moderate Alzheimer’s were monitored overnight for NREM sleep spindles and slow oscillations
Higher CSF orexin levels correlated with faster disease progression across a three‑year follow‑up
Stronger sleep spindle density and longer slow oscillations weakened the orexin‑related decline
CSF orexin concentrations were significantly higher in women than men

mars_heat_anomaly_2026.headline: Mars’ Southern Interior Up to 400°C Hotter Than North, Study Finds
mars_heat_anomaly_2026.summary: Gravity‑based tidal tomography shows Mars’ southern mantle may be 200‑400 °C hotter than the north, hinting at partial melt and past magnetic activity.
highlights: Gravity measurements reveal a temperature gap of 200‑400 °C between the southern and northern mantle
Tidal tomography used data from Mars Global Surveyor, Mars Odyssey, and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
The hotter southern interior could explain anomalous magnetic signatures and faster seismic attenuation observed by InSight

cascadia_megathrust_shaking.headline: Shallower Juan de Fuca Plate May Amplify Oregon’s Next Cascadia Megaquake
cascadia_megathrust_shaking.summary: New seismic data show the Juan de Fuca slab is about 20 km deep off northern Oregon, 5 km shallower than thought, boosting expected shaking by up to 17 %.
highlights: The slab interface is estimated at ~20 km depth, 5 km shallower than previous models
Peak ground acceleration could increase 9‑17 % along the northern Oregon coast
A deep sedimentary basin beneath Tillamook may trap and amplify seismic waves

spacetime_crystal_black_hole.headline: Spacetime Crystal Can Flip Into Microscopic Black Hole, Researchers Show
spacetime_crystal_black_hole.summary: Physicists derived an exact formula showing that a critical spacetime crystal can either dissolve or collapse into a microscopic black hole with a tiny energy shift.
highlights: Researchers from Goethe University Frankfurt and TU Wien derived an analytic solution using an infinite‑dimensional trick.
The formula describes critical collapse of a spacetime crystal that can turn into a black hole after a minute energy addition.
Simulations since 1993 predicted this behavior, but the new work provides the first exact mathematical description.
The method works in the limit of infinitely many dimensions and can be mapped back to our four‑dimensional universe.

new_frog_species_madagascar.headline: Seven New Diamond Frog Species Unveiled from Madagascar’s Forest Floor
new_frog_species_madagascar.summary: Researchers combined field surveys, museum specimens and museomics to describe seven previously unknown Rhombophryne species, boosting known diversity to 27 amid rapid habitat loss.
highlights: Seven new Rhombophryne species identified, raising total to 27.
DNA from century‑old type specimens and fresh samples resolved long‑standing taxonomic confusion.
Findings inform Madagascar’s Biodiversity 30x30 conservation plan and protected‑area proposals.
Study published in peer‑reviewed Vertebrate Zoology (2026) with DOI 10.3897/vz.76.e172567.

nanocrystal_recipe_2026.headline: University of Chicago Unlocks Metal Nitride Nanocrystals for Flexible Electronics
nanocrystal_recipe_2026.summary: Chemists at University of Chicago and Argonne have devised a molten‑salt method that yields nanocrystals from tough metal nitrides, expanding LED, implant and superconductor prospects.
highlights: Nearly a dozen metal‑nitride nanocrystals—including gallium, titanium, niobium and molybdenum nitrides—were synthesized using
The breakthrough relies on molten salts and a precise temperature‑ammonia pressure “sweet spot” that breaks strong
Published in Nature (2026), the method promises printable, polymer‑compatible nanomaterials for LEDs, medical implants and

magnetic_clues_ancient_dust_grains.headline: Ancient Meteorite Grains Reveal Magnetic Field Shaping Sun’s Birth
magnetic_clues_ancient_dust_grains.summary: MIT researchers found that calcium‑aluminum‑rich inclusions in the Antarctic meteorite DOM 08006 preserve the earliest magnetic field of the protosolar nebula, shedding light on the Sun’s formation.
highlights: CAIs from DOM 08006 show magnetization dating to the first 200,000 years of the Solar System
The recorded magnetic field was stronger than Earth’s present field, implying active magnetized winds
Two scenarios were proposed: early‑epoch magnetization or later heating‑event magnetization
Findings suggest magnetic forces, alongside gravity, guided the collapse of the protostellar cloud

2608_28413v1.headline: First Multiply‑Imaged Superluminous Supernova SN 2025wny Observed by HST and JWST
2608_28413v1.summary: Astronomers used Hubble and James Webb to capture five lensed images of SN 2025wny at redshift 2.0151, enabling precise time‑delay measurements for cosmology.
highlights: Five resolved images of SN 2025wny were identified through galaxy‑scale lensing
HST provided ultraviolet photometry while JWST delivered near‑infrared spectroscopy
The system offers the first feasible photometric and spectroscopic time‑delay analysis for a superluminous supernova

2608_28415v1.headline: Gravitationally Lensed Superluminous Supernova SN 2025wny Illuminates Cosmic Noon
2608_28415v1.summary: Astronomers present dense UV‑to‑optical data of SN 2025wny at redshift z = 2.015, revealing unprecedented spectral details and a peak luminosity exceeding 4×10^44 erg s⁻¹.
highlights: SN 2025wny is the most extensively observed high‑redshift SLSN‑I with rest‑frame UV coverage out to +80 days
The event shows a rare FUV continuum excess, plateau, and unusually high black‑body temperatures
Spectra display minimal UV line blanketing, no O II absorption, and hints of C II, Hα, and possible He I

hubble_tension_guide.headline: Mid‑Time Physics May Resolve the Hubble Tension, New Study Shows
hubble_tension_guide.summary: Researchers propose generalized PAge parameterizations that incorporate CMB data, finding mid‑time modifications can alleviate the Hubble tension.
highlights: Generalized PAge (GPAge) models extend to redshifts beyond the CMB surface
GPAge fits outperform standard ΛCDM across all information‑criteria tests
Mid‑time cosmic physics emerges as a promising solution to the Hubble discrepancy

cgem_telescope_design.headline: Canadian Galactic Emission Mapper Begins 8‑10 GHz Polarization Survey of Northern Sky
cgem_telescope_design.summary: The new CGEM radio telescope is now mapping polarized Galactic foregrounds at 8‑10 GHz to support searches for primordial B‑mode signals in the CMB.
highlights: CGEM employs an on‑axis hat‑feed design with exceptional intrinsic polarization purity
Optimized optics reduce T→P leakage to levels far below the expected Cℓ^{BB} for r = 10⁻³ when scaled to 95 GHz
A novel Astroquartz composite secondary mirror provides low loss while preserving optical symmetry

9.headline: First‑Principles Model Links GW170817 Gravitational Waves, GRB170817A Gamma‑Ray Burst, and AT2017gfo Kilonova
9.summary: A comprehensive simulation using general‑relativistic magnetohydrodynamics and neutrino‑radiation transfer reproduces the jet luminosity of ~10^51 erg s⁻¹ and ejecta mass of ~0.08 M⊙ for the GW170817 event.
highlights: Relativistic jet with isotropic‑equivalent luminosity ≈10^51 erg s⁻¹ matches GRB170817A afterglow
Neutron‑rich ejecta of ≈0.08 M⊙ reproduces AT2017gfo kilonova light curves
Simulation integrates merger dynamics, nucleosynthesis, and photon radiative transfer in a single framework

11.headline: JWST/MIRI MRS Maps PAH and Warm H₂ Emission in Eight z≈1 Star‑Forming Galaxies
11.summary: Using JWST’s MIRI MRS, astronomers resolved PAH features and mid‑IR atomic lines across eight z≈1 galaxies, revealing size, charge, and shock signatures linked to AGN and mergers.
highlights: PAH emission detected from 3.3 µm to 11.3 µm across all galaxies
Central PAHs are larger and less ionized than those in outer regions
AGN‑hosting and interacting systems show higher fractions of neutral PAHs and elevated H₂ line ratios

personalized_mrna_vaccine_melanoma_succe.headline: Personalized mRNA Melanoma Vaccine Boosts Field Amid Political Skepticism
personalized_mrna_vaccine_melanoma_succe.summary: Clinical success of Moderna and Merck's personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine offers a hopeful boost for the technology despite lingering vaccine skepticism.
highlights: Moderna and Merck reported positive trial outcomes in patients with melanoma using a personalized mRNA vaccine
The mRNA platform can be reprogrammed to encode virtually any protein, enabling rapid vaccine design
Operation Warp Speed accelerated COVID‑19 vaccine development, laying groundwork for cancer applications
Experts suggest the breakthrough may help soften public stigma around vaccines

fossil_feet_evolution.headline: Monkey Foot Flexibility Challenges Assumptions About Human‑Chimp Ancestor
fossil_feet_evolution.summary: Wild sooty mangabey monkeys in West Africa can bend their midfeet up to 46° while climbing vertical trunks, forcing a rethink of the last common ancestor’s locomotion.
highlights: Mangabeys achieved 46° midfoot flexion despite lacking chimp‑like ankle flexibility
Study by Luke Fannin and W. Scott McGraw appears in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Research shows that monkey‑like feet could still support effective vertical climbing

mars_thermal_anomaly.headline: Mars Southern Mantle Hotter by Up to 750°F Reveals Deep Thermal Anomaly
mars_thermal_anomaly.summary: Analysis of NASA spacecraft gravity data shows the southern mantle of Mars is up to 750 °F hotter than the north, suggesting lingering partial melt.
highlights: Southern mantle temperature exceeds northern mantle by 200‑400 °C (up to 750 °F)
Tidal tomography of Mars Global Surveyor, Odyssey and Reconnaissance Orbiter data uncovered the anomaly
Hotter south may explain faster seismic wave attenuation recorded by InSight and magnetic remnants
Southern crust is ~15.5 mi (25 km) thicker, possibly preserving heat from an ancient giant impact

h5n1_australia_spread.headline: Bird flu threatens Australian wildlife: monitoring key to protect species
h5n1_australia_spread.summary: The lethal H5N1 strain is spreading along southern Australia’s coast, killing wild birds and seals, prompting urgent monitoring to safeguard vulnerable species.
highlights: Infected waterfowl are expected to carry H5N1 inland to shrinking wetlands during El Niño conditions
Macquarie Island’s dense seabird and seal colonies face imminent exposure as researchers are evacuated
Shearwaters returning to Bass Strait islands may suffer massive losses from virus‑laden environments
Scavengers such as foxes and mynas could transport the virus into urban areas, affecting magpies and possums

diamond_piezoelectric.headline: Ultrathin Diamond Membranes Exhibit Unexpected Piezoelectric Power Generation
diamond_piezoelectric.summary: Researchers at the University of Hong Kong have shown that flexible polycrystalline diamond membranes generate repeatable voltage when bent, overturning a century‑old assumption.
highlights: Edge exfoliation produced ultrathin polycrystalline diamond membranes that can flex significantly.
Bending the membranes yields stable voltage signals, confirming intrinsic piezoelectric response.
First‑principles calculations attribute the effect to asymmetry at grain boundaries.
Potential applications include self‑powered medical implants and durable micro‑energy systems.

four_little_red_dot_pairs_hint_at_black_.headline: JWST Uncovers Four Dual 'Little Red Dot' Pairs Hinting at Early Black Hole Mergers
four_little_red_dot_pairs_hint_at_black_.summary: Infrared JWST images reveal four closely spaced Little Red Dot pairs from 12.5‑12.8 billion years ago, suggesting nascent black hole mergers in the early universe.
highlights: Four dual Little Red Dot pairs were identified at separations of only a few thousand to tens of thousands of light‑years.
The new pixel‑by‑pixel color selection method distinguishes close black‑hole candidates missed by conventional techniques.
Statistical analysis shows the likelihood of such close pairings occurring by chance is extremely low.

superconducting_states_hiding.headline: Two Hidden Superconducting States Unveiled in Ultrathin NbSe2 and TaS2
superconducting_states_hiding.summary: Highly sensitive tunneling spectroscopy shows that few‑layer NbSe2 and TaS2 each host two strongly interacting superconducting orders masquerading as a single state.
highlights: NbSe2 and TaS2 exhibit two distinct superconducting orders despite appearing as one
Tunneling spectroscopy revealed the hidden dual‑gap structure
The same dual‑order model explains magnetic‑field responses
Bulk NbSe2 may contain three interacting superconducting orders

peptides_can_form_well_defined_structure.headline: Peptides Fold into Stable Omega‑Loop Structures in Venus‑Like Sulfuric Acid
peptides_can_form_well_defined_structure.summary: MIT researchers show short peptides remain intact and adopt defined three‑dimensional shapes in 98% sulfuric acid, expanding astrobiological habitability scenarios.
highlights: Peptides survive weeks in nearly pure sulfuric acid without hydrolysis
The synthetic seven‑amino‑acid peptide HHQ forms an omega‑loop shape in acid
Similar omega‑loop structures observed for HHQ13 and K7 peptides

percolation_proof_phase_transitions.headline: Zurich Team Proves Supercritical Sharpness for Infinite Transitive Graphs
percolation_proof_phase_transitions.summary: A five‑person group at ETH Zurich delivered a simple proof confirming the supercritical sharpness conjecture for all infinite transitive graphs.

The result settles a decades‑old question about how quickly percolation clusters grow above the critical probability
Their argument uses a novel sprinkling technique to show large isolated pools are virtually impossible
The work builds on earlier sharpness results for lattices and the 2007 subcritical proof by Antunović and Veselić

lead_small_plane_fuel.headline: Lead from Small‑Plane Fuel Found Up to Sevenfold Higher Near Oregon Airports
lead_small_plane_fuel.summary: Researchers used moss biomonitoring and isotopic fingerprinting to show aviation gasoline raises lead concentrations up to seven times in neighborhoods around Hillsboro and Troutdale airports.

lava_world_atmospheres.headline: Stanford Model Shows Lava‑World Exoplanets Retain Atmospheres via Outgassing
lava_world_atmospheres.summary: A peer‑reviewed study reveals that continuous magmatic outgassing can replenish gases lost to stellar radiation, allowing ultra‑hot lava worlds to keep thick atmospheres for billions of years.

The "cosmic sandbar" extends the traditional "cosmic shoreline" boundary
55 Cancri e and TOI‑561 b exhibit thick atmospheres despite extreme proximity
